commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Asana-Siddhi (Stabilization of the seat)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that the physiological stability afforded by a comfortable seat is the foundational prerequisite for higher yoga practices. True yogic progress requires grounding the body to quiet the mind before engaging in pranayama or dharana.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern life, this underscores the necessity of physical comfort and ergonomics as a preliminary to mindfulness and meditation, preventing the distraction caused by physical agitation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Establishment of the physical body in a steady posture, followed by controlled breathing (Puraka) through the Pingala nadi.
commentary_faqs.answer: आसन-सिद्धि (Asana-Siddhi) through Sthira-Sukha (stability and comfort) in preparation for Pranayama.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychological grounding; the use of physical alignment to regulate autonomic nervous system states, emphasizing that mental tranquility is contingent upon bodily stillness.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
आ केशादिति । केशान् मर्यादीकृत्य आ केशात्; नखाग्रान् मर्यादीकृत्य आ नखाग्रात्, निरोधस्य वायोरवरोधस्य अवधिः मर्यादा यस्मिन् कर्मणि तत्तथा कुम्भ्येत् । केशपर्यन्तं नखाग्रपर्यन्तं च वायोः निरोधो यथा भवेत् तथा अतिप्रयत्नेन कुम्भकं कुर्यादित्यर्थः । ननु -
‘हठानिरुद्धः प्राणोऽयं रोमकूपेषु निस्सरेत् ।
ततः प्रत्यायितव्योऽसौ क्रमेणारण्यहस्तिवत् ।
करोति शास्तृनिर्देशात् न च तां परिलङ्घयेत् ।
गृहीतः सेव्यमानस्तु विश्रम्भमुपगच्छति । ’
इति वाक्यविरुद्धमतिप्रयत्नेन कुम्भकं कुर्यादिति कथमुक्तमिति चेन्न -हठान्निरुद्धः प्राणोऽयमिति वाक्यस्य बलादचिरेण प्राणजयं करिष्यामीति बुध्यरम्भ एव । बह्वभ्यासासक्तपरत्वात् क्रमेणारण्यहस्तिवदिति दृष्टान्तस्वारस्याच्च । अत एव सूर्याचन्द्रमासोरभ्यासे ‘धारयित्वा यथाशक्ति’ (३.२१) निधारयेदिति निरोधत इति चोक्तं सङ्गच्छते । तस्मात् कुम्भकस्त्वतिप्रयत्नपूर्वकं कर्तव्यः । यथा यथा अतिप्रयत्नेन कुम्भ्कः क्रियते तथा तथा तस्मिन् गुणाधिक्यं भवेत् । यथा यथा च शिथिलः कुम्भकः स्यात् तथा तथा च गुणाल्पत्वं स्यात् । अत्र योगिनामनुभवोऽपि मानम् । पूरकस्तु शनैः शनैः कार्यः, वेगाद्वा कर्तव्यः । वेगदपि कृते पूरके दोषाभावात् । रेचकस्तु शनैः शनैः एव कर्तव्यः । वेगात् कृते रेचके बलहानिप्रसङ्गात् । ततः शनैः शनैरेव रेचयेत् न तु वेगतः इत्याद्यनेकधा ग्रन्थकारोक्तेश्च । ततो निरोधवधि कुम्भकानन्तरं शनैः शनैः मन्दं मन्दं सव्ये वामभागे स्थिता नाडी सव्यनाडी तया सव्यनाड्या इडया पवनं वायुं रेचयेत् बहिर्निस्सारयेत् । पुनः शनैरित्युक्तिस्तु शनैरेव रेचयेदित्यवधारणार्था । तदुक्तम् -
विस्मये च विषादे च दैन्ये चैवावधारणे ।
commentaries.text:
आ केशादिति । केशान् मर्यादीकृत्य आ केशात्; नखाग्रान् मर्यादीकृत्य आ नखाग्रात्, निरोधस्य वायोरवरोधस्य अवधिः मर्यादा यस्मिन् कर्मणि तत्तथा कुम्भ्येत् । केशपर्यन्तं नखाग्रपर्यन्तं च वायोः निरोधो यथा भवेत् तथा अतिप्रयत्नेन कुम्भकं कुर्यादित्यर्थः । ननु -
‘हठानिरुद्धः प्राणोऽयं रोमकूपेषु निस्सरेत् ।
ततः प्रत्यायितव्योऽसौ क्रमेणारण्यहस्तिवत् ।
करोति शास्तृनिर्देशात् न च तां परिलङ्घयेत् ।
गृहीतः सेव्यमानस्तु विश्रम्भमुपगच्छति । ’
इति वाक्यविरुद्धमतिप्रयत्नेन कुम्भकं कुर्यादिति कथमुक्तमिति चेन्न -हठान्निरुद्धः प्राणोऽयमिति वाक्यस्य बलादचिरेण प्राणजयं करिष्यामीति बुध्यरम्भ एव । बह्वभ्यासासक्तपरत्वात् क्रमेणारण्यहस्तिवदिति दृष्टान्तस्वारस्याच्च । अत एव सूर्याचन्द्रमासोरभ्यासे ‘धारयित्वा यथाशक्ति’ (३.२१) निधारयेदिति निरोधत इति चोक्तं सङ्गच्छते । तस्मात् कुम्भकस्त्वतिप्रयत्नपूर्वकं कर्तव्यः । यथा यथा अतिप्रयत्नेन कुम्भ्कः क्रियते तथा तथा तस्मिन् गुणाधिक्यं भवेत् । यथा यथा च शिथिलः कुम्भकः स्यात् तथा तथा च गुणाल्पत्वं स्यात् । अत्र योगिनामनुभवोऽपि मानम् । पूरकस्तु शनैः शनैः कार्यः, वेगाद्वा कर्तव्यः । वेगदपि कृते पूरके दोषाभावात् । रेचकस्तु शनैः शनैः एव कर्तव्यः । वेगात् कृते रेचके बलहानिप्रसङ्गात् । ततः शनैः शनैरेव रेचयेत् न तु वेगतः इत्याद्यनेकधा ग्रन्थकारोक्तेश्च । ततो निरोधवधि कुम्भकानन्तरं शनैः शनैः मन्दं मन्दं सव्ये वामभागे स्थिता नाडी सव्यनाडी तया सव्यनाड्या इडया पवनं वायुं रेचयेत् बहिर्निस्सारयेत् । पुनः शनैरित्युक्तिस्तु शनैरेव रेचयेदित्यवधारणार्था । तदुक्तम् -
विस्मये च विषादे च दैन्ये चैवावधारणे ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary explains that 'a-keshat' and 'a-nakhagrat' set the limits of the practice. One should practice Kumbhaka with great effort (atiprayatna) such that the restraint of breath is felt everywhere from the hair follicles to the nail tips. While some texts warn against forced restraint (likening it to a wild elephant that must be tamed gradually), the commentator reconciles this by stating that the goal is sincere, persistent practice. The efficacy of Kumbhaka increases with the intensity of the effort applied. It further distinguishes that while Puraka (inhalation) can be done quickly or slowly, Rechaka (exhalation) must be performed slowly to prevent loss of bodily strength, concluding with the necessity of controlled exhalation through the Ida nadi.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: भाष्यकार का आशय है कि 'आ केशात्' और 'आ नखाग्रात्' मर्यादा का निर्धारण करते हैं। कुम्भक का अभ्यास इतनी अतिप्रयत्नपूर्वक (तीव्रता के साथ) करना चाहिए कि प्राण का निरोध केशों से लेकर नखों तक व्याप्त हो जाए। यद्यपि हठयोग के अन्य वचनों में धीरे-धीरे अभ्यास करने का निर्देश है, तथापि यहाँ अतिप्रयत्न का समर्थन किया गया है क्योंकि अभ्यास की सघनता ही सिद्धि का कारण है। भाष्य में यह भी स्पष्ट किया गया है कि पूरक वेग से किया जा सकता है, किन्तु रेचक सदैव धीरे-धीरे ही होना चाहिए ताकि शारीरिक बल का ह्रास न हो।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Kumbhaka Intensity
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the total bodily engagement during breath retention. It argues that the effectiveness of Kumbhaka is directly proportional to the intensity of the effort applied, aiming to permeate the prana throughout the entire physical sheath.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the ancient understanding of the interconnectedness of breath and the nervous system, suggesting that controlled, intense focus (Kumbhaka) bridges the gap between mechanical breathing and physiological mastery.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Kumbhaka (retention), Puraka (controlled inhalation), and slow, steady Rechaka (exhalation) through the Ida nadi.
commentary_faqs.answer: Pranayama-Siddhi through Atiprayatna (intense effort) where the Vayu-Nirodha encompasses the entire Sharira (body) from Kesha to Nakhagra.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this equates to 'focused intent'—the correlation between cognitive effort and physiological outcome. In modern somatic practices, this reinforces how controlled respiratory interventions influence the autonomic nervous system.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: कपालशोधनमिति । कपालस्य मस्तकस्य शोधनं शुद्धिकरं वातजा दोषा वातदोषा अशीतिप्रकाराः तान् हन्तीति वातदोषघ्नं कृमीणामुदरे जातानां दोषो विकारः तं हरतीति कृमिदोषहृत् । पुनः पुनः भूयो भूयः कार्यम् । सूर्येणापूर्य कुम्भयित्वा चन्द्रेण रेचनमिति रीत्या इदमुत्तमम् उत्कृष्टं सूर्यभेदनं सूर्यभेदनाख्यमुक्तं योगिभिरिति शेषः ॥ ५० ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding 'Kapala-shodhanam': It is that which purifies the Kapala, i.e., the cranium/head. 'Vata-dosha-ghnam': It destroys the eighty types of Vata-related imbalances. 'Krimi-dosha-hrit': It removes the doshas or disorders caused by worms (parasites) developed in the abdomen. This should be performed again and again. According to the method of filling (puraka) through the sun (right nostril) and exhaling (rechaka) through the moon (left nostril), this is termed 'Suryabhedana', which is proclaimed by the Yogis as an excellent practice.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: कपालशोधनमिति - कपाल का अर्थ है मस्तक, उसका शोधन करने वाला। वातजा दोषा वातदोषाः अर्थात् वात संबंधी अस्सी प्रकार के रोगों को जो नष्ट करता है, वह वातदोषघ्न है। कृमिदोषहृत् का अर्थ है उदर में उत्पन्न कृमियों के कारण जो विकार होते हैं, उनका नाश करने वाला। इसे बार-बार करना चाहिए। सूर्य (दाहिने) स्वर से पूरक करके और चन्द्र (बाएँ) स्वर से रेचन करने की रीति को योगियों ने सूर्यभेदन कहा है, जो कि अत्यंत उत्कृष्ट है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse highlights the physiological purification benefits of Suryabhedana Pranayama. By purifying the 'Kapala' (skull) and balancing Vata, the practice facilitates mental clarity and physical homeostasis.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These ancient physiological insights correlate with modern understanding of respiratory health and the importance of clearing nasal passages to improve oxygen intake and reduce systemic inflammation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice is Suryabhedana Pranayama: inhaling through the Pingala (Sun) Nadi and exhaling through the Ida (Moon) Nadi.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Kaphadosha and Vatadosha regulation via Nadi Shodhana based on the Suryabhedana technique, utilizing the prana-vayu to remove internal toxins (krimi).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological relevance lies in the autonomic nervous system regulation; stimulating the sympathetic nervous system through specific breathing patterns aids in detoxification and metabolic efficiency.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: उज्जायिनमाह सार्धेन - मुखमिति । मुखम् आस्यं संयमं कृत्वा मुद्रयित्वा इत्यर्थः । कण्ठात्तु कण्ठादारभ्य हृदयावधि हृदयमवधिः यस्मिन् कर्मणि तत्तथा स्वनेन सहितं यथा स्यात् तथा । उभे क्रियाविशेषणे । लगति श्लिष्यति पवन इत्यर्थात् । तथा तेन प्रकारेण नाडीभ्याम् इडापिङ्गलाभ्यां पवनं वायुं शनैः मन्दमाकृष्य आकृष्टं कृत्वा पूरयित्वा इत्यर्थः । प्राणं पूर्ववत् पूर्वेण सूर्यभेदनेन तुल्यं पूर्ववत् । आकेशादानखाग्राच्च निरोधावधि कुम्भयेदित्युक्तरीत्या कुम्भयेद् रोधयेत् । ततः कुम्भकान्तरमिडया वामनाड्या रेचयेत् त्यजेत् ॥ ५१ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text explains Ujjayi in one and a half verses. 'Mukham' means the mouth; having controlled it, one should seal it. 'Kanthattu' means starting from the throat, and 'hridayavadhi' means up to the heart as the limit; this implies the breath should be accompanied by sound within that space. Both are adverbs of the action. 'Lagati' implies the breath touches the throat. In that manner, one should slowly draw the breath (Pavam) through both nadis (Ida and Pingala). 'Pranam' (the breath) should be managed as in the previously described Surya-bhedana; one should hold the breath (Kumbhayet) as per the rule 'from hair to toes.' Then, exhale through the left nadi (Ida).

'Kanthattu' means starting from the throat, and 'hridayavadhi' means up to the heart as the limit; this implies the breath should be accompanied by sound within that space. 'Pranam' (the breath) should be managed as in the previously described Surya-bhedana; one should hold the breath (Kumbhayet) as per the rule 'from hair to toes.' Then, exhale through the left nadi (Ida).

commentaries.description: सार्ध श्लोक से उज्जयी का वर्णन है। मुख को संयम करके, अर्थात् बंद करके। कण्ठ से हृदय तक के मार्ग में शब्द के साथ वायु का संचरण हो। 'लगति' अर्थात् वायु कण्ठ का स्पर्श करे। उसी प्रकार इडा और पिंगला नाड़ियों से धीरे-धीरे वायु को आकृष्ट करे। सूर्यभेदन के समान ही यहाँ कुम्भक करे (आकेशादानखाग्रात् की रीति से)। तत्पश्चात इडा नाड़ी से रेचन (त्याग) करे।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Prana-Samyama
commentary_faqs.answer: Ujjayi is a yogic technique involving the constriction of the glottis to produce sound, balancing the flow of Prana within the subtle nervous system. It serves to pacify the mind and regulate the vital energy (Prana) between the Ida and Pingala nadis.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, Ujjayi serves as a foundational technique for stress reduction, lowering heart rate, and promoting autonomic nervous system balance, widely used in both therapeutic yoga and meditative practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Mukh-samyama (sealing the mouth), Kanth-gharsan (throat constriction/sound), Ida-Pingala-sancharan (breath flow regulation), and Kumbhaka (breath retention).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on Prana-vayu-nirodha (restraint of vital air) through the modulation of the Kanthasthana (throat region) using sound-resonance (svara-sahit) to achieve internal stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern clinical studies affirm that controlled breath-holding and the subtle vibrations in the throat (vagus nerve stimulation) can activate the parasympathetic nervous system, providing immediate relief from anxiety and autonomic dysregulation.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
उज्जायिगुणानाह सार्धश्लोकेन - श्लेष्मदोषहरमिति । कण्ठे कण्ठप्रदेशे श्लेष्मणो दोषाः श्लेष्मदोषाः कासादयः तान् हरतीति श्लोष्मदोषहरः तं देहानलस्य देहमध्यगतस्य अनलस्य जाठरस्य विवर्धनं विशेषेण वर्धनं दीपनमित्यर्थः ॥ ५२ ॥
नाडीति । नाडी शिरा जलं पीतमुदकमुदरं तुन्दमासमन्तात् देहे वर्तमाना धातवः आधातवः । एषामितरेतरद्वन्द्वः । तेषु गतः प्राप्तः यो दोषः विकारः तं विशेषेण नाशयतीति नाडीजलोदराधातुगतदोषविनशनम् । गच्छता गमनं कुर्वता तिष्ठता स्थितेन वापि पुंसा उज्जायाख्यम् उज्जायीत्याख्या यस्य तत् । तु इत्यनेन अस्य वैशिष्ट्यं द्योतयति । कार्यं कर्तव्यम् । उज्जापीति क्वचित् पाठः । गच्छता तिष्ठता तु बन्धरहितः कर्तव्यः । कुम्भकशब्दः स्त्रीलिङ्गः । पुल्लिङ्गपाठे तु विशेषणेष्वपि पुल्लिङ्गः पाठः कार्यः ॥ ५३ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentator describes the qualities of Ujjayi. It destroys phlegmatic defects (shleshma-dosha) such as cough located in the throat. It enhances the internal fire (Jatharagni) residing in the center of the body. Regarding 'nadi-jala-udara-dhatu-gata-dosha-vinasanam': The Nadi (channels), Jala (ingested fluids), Udara (abdomen), and Dhatu (bodily tissues) are the sites where defects reside; Ujjayi destroys these. It should be performed by the practitioner whether walking or standing.

commentary_faqs.answer: This verse addresses the therapeutic effect of the Ujjayi Pranayama on the physical body, positing that it clears metabolic, fluidic, and structural imbalances. It functions as a physiological purifier that balances the internal fire (Jatharagni) and cleanses the energetic pathways.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this relates to detoxification and the management of psychosomatic stress, emphasizing the link between regulated breathing and systemic bodily homeostasis.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Ujjayi Pranayama performed while standing or walking, which facilitates the removal of phlegmatic obstructions and digestive stimulation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Dosha-hara (remover of impurities) refers to the restoration of equilibrium across bodily channels (nadi), fluid metabolism (jala), abdominal health (udara), and tissue health (dhatu) through the regulation of prana.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: The practice represents a sophisticated early biological model of systemic detoxification, suggesting that rhythmic breathing exercises influence the autonomous nervous system and metabolic processes.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: सीत्कारीकुम्भ्कमाह - सीत्कामिति । वक्त्रे मुखे सीत्कां सीदेव सीत्का सीदिति शब्दः सीत्कारः तां कुर्यात् । ओष्ठयोरन्तरे संलग्नया जिह्वया सीत्कारपूर्वकं मुखे पूरकं कुर्यादित्यर्थः । घ्राणेनैव नासिकयैव इत्यनेन उभाभ्यां नासापुटाभ्यां रेचकः कार्यः इत्युक्तम् । एवशब्देन वक्त्रस्य व्यवच्छेदः । वक्त्रेण वायोः निस्सारणं त्वभ्यासानन्तरमपि न कार्यम् । बलहानिकरत्वात् । विजृम्भिकां रेचकं कुर्यादित्यत्रापि संबध्यते । कुम्भकस्त्वनुक्तोऽपि सीत्कार्याः कुम्म्भकत्वादेवावगन्तव्यः । अथ सीत्कार्याः प्रशंसा । एवमुक्तप्रकारेण अभ्यासः पौनः पुन्येन अनुष्ठानं स एव योगः योगसाधनत्वात् तेन द्वितीयः एव द्वितीयकः कामदेवः कन्दर्पः । रूपलावण्यातिशयेन कामदेवसादृश्यात् ॥ ५४ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Describing the Sītkārī Kumbhaka: 'Sītkār' means the sound produced by the teeth. One should perform the inhalation through the mouth with a hissing sound by keeping the tongue slightly between the lips. The word 'ghrāṇenaiva' (only through the nostrils) implies that exhalation must be performed through both nostrils; the word 'eva' excludes the mouth for exhalation. Exhaling through the mouth should not be done even after practice, as it causes a loss of strength. One should perform 'vijṛmbhikā' (yawning/releasing air) as part of the process. Although 'Kumbhaka' is not explicitly stated, it is understood because it is named 'Sītkārī-Kumbhaka'. Regarding the praise of Sītkārī: through repeated practice (abhyāsa), one becomes like Kandarpa (Cupid) due to the excellence of form and grace attained.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: सीत्कारी कुम्भक का वर्णन करते हैं - सीत्कारी अर्थात दाँतों से निकलने वाली ध्वनि। मुख द्वारा जिह्वा को ओष्ठों के बीच रखकर सीत्-सीत् की ध्वनि के साथ पूरक (श्वास लेना) करना चाहिए। 'घ्राणेनैव' (नासिका से ही) कहने का अर्थ है कि रेचक (श्वास छोड़ना) दोनों नासिका छिद्रों से ही करना चाहिए; यहाँ 'एव' शब्द मुख से रेचक का निषेध करता है। अभ्यास के बाद भी मुख से वायु का निष्कासन नहीं करना चाहिए, क्योंकि इससे बल की हानि होती है। कुम्भक का स्पष्ट उल्लेख न होने पर भी, यह सीत्कारी के 'कुम्भक' होने से ही सिद्ध है। सीत्कारी की प्रशंसा में कहा गया है कि निरंतर अभ्यास से साधक रूप और लावण्य में कामदेव (कन्दर्प) के समान हो जाता है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Hatha Yoga Technique
commentary_faqs.answer: Sītkārī is a specialized cooling breath technique described in Hatha Yoga texts. By producing a hissing sound through the teeth or tongue, the practitioner balances internal heat and controls the vital energy (Prana) through precise inhalation and exhalation.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Practiced today for its therapeutic benefits in regulating body temperature, reducing anxiety, and calming the nervous system, it remains a cornerstone of traditional yogic hygiene.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include: 1. Controlled Pūraka via Sītkāra (hissing sound), 2. Restriction of exhalation (Recaka) to nasal passages only, 3. Strict avoidance of oral exhalation to prevent 'balahāni' (loss of vitality), 4. Consistent 'abhyāsa' (repeated practice).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Sītkārī is a specialized form of Prāṇāyāma where the *Pūraka* (inhalation) is generated via a *sīt-kāra* (hissing sound) produced by the tongue and teeth, serving as a distinct technique to channel *Prāṇa* and achieve *Śarīra-Lāvaṇya* (bodily radiance).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern applications focus on the psychological regulation of the autonomic nervous system. The cooling effect of the Sītkārī breath is used as a bio-feedback mechanism to mitigate 'stress-induced heat' or hyper-arousal, promoting emotional stability and physical endurance.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: योगिनीनां चक्रं योगिनीचक्रं योगिनीसमूहः । तस्य संमान्यः संसेव्यः । सृष्टिः प्रपञ्चोत्पत्तिः, संहारः तल्लयःतयोः कारकः कर्ता । क्षुधा भोक्तुमिच्छा न । तृषा जलपानेच्छा न । निद्रा सुषुप्तिः नः । आलस्यं कायचित्तगौरवात् प्रवृत्त्यभावः । कायगौरवं कफादिना चित्तगौरवं तमोगुणेन । नैव प्रजायते नैव प्रादुर्भवति । एवमभ्यासयोगेनेति प्राजायत इति च प्रतिवाक्यं सम्बध्यते ॥ ५५ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Yoginicakra means the cycle or group of Yoginis. He is honored and served by them. Srishti refers to the emergence of the manifest universe; Samhara refers to its dissolution. He is the doer (Karta) of both. Hunger is the desire to eat; thirst is the desire to drink; sleep is deep unconsciousness; sloth is the lack of initiative due to heaviness of body and mind. Heaviness of body is caused by phlegm (Kapha), and heaviness of mind by the quality of darkness (Tamas). These do not manifest in Him at all. By the practice of Yoga (abhyasayoga), all these states are negated as implied in the following sentences.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: योगिनीचक्र का अर्थ है योगिनियों का चक्र या समूह। वे (ईश्वर) उनके द्वारा सम्मानित और सेवित हैं। सृष्टि का अर्थ है प्रपंच की उत्पत्ति, संहार का अर्थ है उसका लय। वे इन दोनों के कर्ता हैं। क्षुधा अर्थात खाने की इच्छा नहीं है, तृषा अर्थात जल पीने की इच्छा नहीं है, निद्रा अर्थात सुषुप्ति नहीं है। आलस्य का अर्थ है काय और चित्त के गौरव (भारीपन) के कारण प्रवृत्ति का अभाव। काय का गौरव कफ आदि के कारण होता है और चित्त का गौरव तमोगुण के कारण। वे (परमात्मा में) उत्पन्न नहीं होते। अभ्यासयोग के द्वारा यह जानना चाहिए कि ये सब क्रियाएँ (विकार) उनमें नहीं हैं।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ishvara-tattva (The Divine Principle)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse establishes the Supreme Being as both the object of veneration for cosmic powers (Yoginis) and the causal agent behind the cyclical manifestation and retraction of the universe. It emphasizes the absolute power of the Divine in overseeing the cosmic order.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the integration of Tantric iconography (Yogini-cakra) with classical Vedantic cosmology, emphasizing the unity of the Divine in both creative and destructive aspects.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Abhyasa-yoga (persistent practice of meditation/discipline) as the path to transcend the Kleshas and physical limitations described in the bhashya.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Ishvara' as the Nitya-mukta (eternally liberated) being who transcends the biological limitations of hunger, thirst, and Guna-based heaviness (Tamas-Kapha).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this verse addresses the 'heaviness' of the mind and body (lethargy, anxiety, and desire-driven behavior), suggesting that steady practice leads to a state of equilibrium and transcendence over the involuntary impulses of the psychosomatic organism.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: भवेदिति । देहस्य शरीरस्य सत्त्वं बलं च भवेत् । अनेन उक्तेन विधिना अभ्यासविधिना योगीन्द्रः योगिनामिन्द्र इव योगीन्द्रः भूमिमण्डले सर्वैरुपद्रवैः विवर्जितः सर्वोपद्रवविवर्जितो भवेत् सत्यम् । ‘सर्वं वाक्यं सावधारणम्’ इति न्यायात् । यदुक्तं फलं तत्सत्यमेव इत्यर्थः ॥ ५६ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding 'Bhavet': The 'sattva' (strength/vitality) of the 'dehasya' (body) should manifest. Through the previously mentioned method—the method of practice (abhyāsa)—the 'Yogindra' (Lord of Yogis, one who is like an emperor among yogis) becomes 'sarvopadravavivarjitaḥ' (completely free from all afflictions) upon the earth. Per the maxim 'Sarvaṃ vākyaṃ sāvadhāraṇam' (all statements [in scriptures] carry an emphatic assurance), the fruit described herein is certainly true.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Deha-Sattva (Vitality of the physical frame) and Abādhatā (Absence of obstacles).
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights the necessity of bodily integrity as a foundation for higher yogic attainment. Sattva here refers to a refined, energized state of the physical form that is immune to external and internal disturbances.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this concept translates to psychosomatic well-being and stress-resilience, emphasizing that a balanced physiology is the prerequisite for mental clarity and spiritual stability.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice prescribed is 'Abhyasa-vidhi' (consistent yogic repetition), which acts as the transformative agent for achieving bodily purification.
commentary_faqs.answer: The Bhashya emphasizes the 'Sattva' (vitality) of the 'Deha' and the attainment of 'Sarvopadravavivarjitatvam' (a state free from all worldly and physiological obstacles) through the authority of the 'Abhyasa-vidhi'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: It suggests the psychological concept of self-actualization, where consistent practice (abhyasa) leads to a state of 'flow' and immunity to environmental stressors.

commentaries.description: शीतली कुम्भक का वर्णन करते हुए कहते हैं: जिह्वा को ओष्ठों से बाहर निकालकर, पक्षी की चोंच के समान बनाकर, उसके द्वारा वायु को खींचना, यही पूरक का अर्थ है। पूर्ववत् (सूर्यभेदन के समान) कुम्भक का साधन करना चाहिए। सुधी (सुष्ठु धीः यस्य) अर्थात विवेकी पुरुष। दोनों नासिका-छिद्रों से धीरे-धीरे पवन का रेचन करना चाहिए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama (Sheetali)
commentary_faqs.answer: Sheetali Pranayama is a cooling breathing technique that balances internal heat and calms the nervous system. By shaping the tongue, the practitioner draws in prana, utilizing the cooling effect of the oral cavity and breath retention to regulate physiological metabolic rates.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, it serves as a powerful tool for stress reduction and managing sympathetic nervous system overdrive. Its physiological effect is recognized for lowering blood pressure and inducing a parasympathetic state of deep relaxation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Jihvā-saṅkocana (tongue curling), Pūraka (inhalation), Kumbhaka (retention), Recaka (exhalation). The practice requires a slow and gradual rhythm (śanakaiḥ) to ensure internal balance.
commentary_faqs.answer: Sheetali Pranayama involves specific anatomical shaping of the tongue (jihvā) to achieve śītalatā (coolness). The bhashya underscores the continuity of the practice, linking it to established methodologies of Kumbhaka, reinforcing that wisdom (sudhī) is required to calibrate the duration and intensity of the breath.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this technique acts as a 'biological brake' for the nervous system. By consciously slowing the respiratory rate and cooling the air, one can disrupt the cycle of anxiety and hyper-arousal, providing a self-regulatory mechanism for emotional homeostasis.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: शीतलीगुणानाह - गुल्मश्च प्लीहश्च गुल्मप्लीहौ रोगविशेषौ आदी येषां ते गुल्मप्लीहादिकाः तान् , रोगान् आमयान् , ज्वरं ज्वराख्यं रोगं , पित्तं पित्तविकारं, क्षुधां भोक्तुमिच्छां , तृषां जलपानेच्छां, विषाणि सर्पादिविषजनितविकारान् । शीतली, नाम इति प्रसिद्धार्थकमव्ययम् । इयमुक्ता कुम्भिका निहन्ति नितरां हन्ति । कुम्भशब्दः स्त्रीलिङ्गोऽपि । तथा च श्रीहर्षः - ‘उदरस्य कुम्भीरथ शातकुम्भाजाः’ । (नै.च ५.१९) इति ॥ ५८ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary introduces the cooling (śītalī) properties: Gulma (abdominal mass) and Plīha (spleen) are specific types of diseases; 'ādikān' refers to those diseases beginning with these. 'Rogān' refers to ailments. 'Jvaram' refers to the disease known as fever. 'Pittam' refers to biliary disorders. 'Kṣudhā' refers to the desire to eat, and 'Tṛṣā' refers to the desire for water. 'Śītalī' is a particle indicating a well-known name. This mentioned Kumbhika plant completely destroys these conditions. The word 'Kumbha' is also feminine in usage, as Sriharsha mentions: 'Udarasya kumbhīratha śātakumbhājah'.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: शीतली (शीतल करने वाले) गुणों का वर्णन करते हुए भाष्यकार कहते हैं - गुल्म और प्लीहा ये रोग विशेष हैं, आदि शब्द से ऐसे ही अन्य रोगों का ग्रहण है। 'रोगान्' का अर्थ व्याधियाँ है, 'ज्वरम्' ज्वर नामक रोग है, 'पित्तम्' पित्त के विकार हैं, 'क्षुधा' खाने की इच्छा है और 'तृषा' जल पीने की इच्छा है। 'शीतली' नाम प्रसिद्धार्थवाचक अव्यय है। यह वर्णित कुम्भिका औषधि इन सबको पूर्णतः नष्ट कर देती है। 'कुम्भ' शब्द का प्रयोग स्त्रीलिंग में भी होता है, जैसा कि श्रीहर्ष ने नैषधीयचरित में कहा है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ayurvedic Therapeutics and Pathological Mitigation
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse outlines the therapeutic efficacy of a medicinal substance (Kumbhika) in addressing specific metabolic and inflammatory conditions. It highlights the Ayurvedic perspective on internal organ health (gulma and plīha) as foundational to systemic wellness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This illustrates the integration of botanical knowledge into traditional healing systems, where specific plants are classified by their ability to correct dosha imbalances (pitta) and physiological distress (fever, hunger, thirst).

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice involves the administration of the 'Kumbhika' herb, recognized in Ayurveda for its specific therapeutic potency in cooling the body and resolving chronic internal blockages.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Dravyaguna' (pharmacology) and the efficacy of 'Shitali' (cooling) agents in pacifying 'Pitta' (bilious fire) and 'Gulma-Pliha' (organ-related pathologies).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern terms, this reflects the psychological and physiological benefits of maintaining homeostatic balance, specifically managing inflammation and metabolic cravings through natural, non-invasive means.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: भस्त्राकुम्भकस्य पद्मासनपूर्वकमेव अनुष्ठानात् तदादौ पद्मासनमाह - ऊर्वोरिति । उपर्युत्ताने शुभे शुद्धे उभे द्वे पादयोः तले अधः प्रदेशौ ऊर्वोः संस्थाप्य सम्यक् स्थापयित्वा वसेत् । एतत् पद्मासनं भवेत् । कीदृशं सर्वेषां पापानां प्रकर्षेण नाशकम् । अत्र उपरि इत्यव्ययम् उत्तानवाचकम् । तथा च कारकेषु मनोरमायाम् - ‘उपर्युपरि बुद्धीनाम्’ इत्यत्र उपरिबुद्धीनामित्यस्य उत्तानबुद्धीनामिति व्याख्यानं कृतम् ॥ ५९ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Since Bhastrika-kumbhaka must be performed only after assuming Padmasana, the text first describes Padmasana starting with 'Ūrvoh'. By placing both soles of the feet upwards on the opposite thighs, one should sit correctly. This is known as Padmasana. What kind of posture is it? It is the one that thoroughly destroys all sins. Here, the indeclinable 'upari' denotes 'uttana' (upward-facing). In the Manoramā text under the section on Karakas, the phrase 'uparyupari buddhīnām' has been explained as 'uttana-buddhīnām'.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: चूँकि भस्त्राकुम्भक का अनुष्ठान पद्मासनपूर्वक ही करना चाहिए, अतः सबसे पहले पद्मासन का वर्णन करते हुए कहते हैं - 'ऊर्वोः' इत्यादि। दोनों पैरों के तलवों को एक-दूसरे की जांघों पर ऊपर की ओर करके भली-भांति बैठकर जो स्थिति बनती है, वह पद्मासन है। यह कैसा आसन है? यह सभी पापों का विनाश करने वाला है। यहाँ 'उपरि' अव्यय 'उत्तान' (ऊपर की ओर) का वाचक है। इसी प्रकार मनोरमा के कारक प्रकरण में 'उपर्युपरि बुद्धीनाम्' का अर्थ 'उत्तानबुद्धीनाम्' किया गया है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama Preparatory Ritual
commentary_faqs.answer: Bhastrika is a vital Hatha Yoga practice involving rapid, forceful inhalations and exhalations. It is intended to invigorate the internal fire (Agni) and purify the Nadis, setting the physiological foundation for deeper meditative states.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, Bhastrika is widely used as a therapeutic tool for increasing respiratory efficiency and mental alertness, often categorized within mindfulness and stress-management practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Padmasana (the posture), steady sitting (āsana), and preparatory postural alignment (sthāpanā) are the primary practices highlighted as essential conditions for breathwork.
commentary_faqs.answer: The bhashya emphasizes the 'pūrvaka' (prerequisite) nature of Asana in the context of Pranayama, specifically highlighting 'Padmasana' as the substrate for 'Bhastrika' and its role in 'pāpānāṃ prakarṣeṇa nāśakam' (thorough destruction of impurities/sins).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: The text demonstrates the psychosomatic link between stable, erect posture and the regulation of metabolic processes, which is crucial for modern psychological interventions focusing on body-mind grounding.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Describing the Bhastrika-Kumbhaka: The phrase 'samyak' implies correctly. 'Griva' (neck) and 'udara' (abdomen) together form the compound 'grivodaram' (using the ekavadbhava rule for limbs). 'Samagrivodarah' means one whose neck and abdomen are in a straight line. 'Sudhi' means one whose intellect is stable. Having properly and steadily assumed the Padmasana, and having controlled the facial expressions and senses, one should exert effort to exhale the Prana (internal air) through one of the nostrils.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: भस्त्रिका कुम्भक के संदर्भ में 'सम्यक्' का अर्थ उचित रूप से है। ग्रीवा और उदर का समाहार 'ग्रीवोदर' है (प्राणि के अंगों के कारण एकवद्भाव हुआ है)। समग्रीवोदर का अर्थ है जिसके गले और पेट की स्थिति सीधी हो। 'सुधी' का अर्थ है जिसकी बुद्धि सुस्थिर है। पद्मासन को भली-भांति स्थिर करके, मुख को संयमित कर, प्रयत्नपूर्वक नासिका के एक छिद्र से शरीर के भीतर स्थित प्राण (वायु) को रेचित करना चाहिए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Sthira-Asana (Postural Stability)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that physical alignment is the prerequisite for meditative and pranic practices. By establishing a stable, upright posture, the practitioner ensures the unobstructed flow of prana through the sushumna nadi.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern terms, this reflects the psychosomatic connection where structural alignment of the spine positively impacts autonomic nervous system regulation and cognitive focus.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Padmasana (Lotus posture), Griva-Udara-Samatva (Alignment of the spine and abdomen), and Prana-Rechana (Exhalation).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept relies on 'Deha-Samyama' (physical control) and 'Ekavadbhava' (the grammatical linguistic rule of grouping physical limbs) to define the anatomical requirement for 'Kumbhaka'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the correlation between 'Posture and Mental Clarity' (Sudhi). Maintaining a straight posture is a fundamental technique for reducing stress and increasing parasympathetic activity, essential for psychological well-being.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary describes the method of exhalation (Rechaka). 'Hṛtkaṇṭhe' refers to the heart and the throat; this is a collective dual compound. 'Kapālāvadhi' means up to the skull. 'Sasvanam' means along with the sound. The implied word is 'prāṇa' (the breath). One should exhale in this specific manner. The passage further explains filling the air (pūraṇam) from the heart lotus with speed (tarasā). The word 'cāpi' is added to complete the poetic rhythm (pādapūraṇārtham).

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama (Breath Regulation)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the technique of 'Rechaka' (exhalation) in the context of advanced breath control. It emphasizes internalizing the movement of breath as a sonic experience connecting the physical centers (heart, throat, skull) to achieve internal energetic resonance.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This practice highlights the ancient understanding of the mind-breath connection, relevant today for stress management, focus, and deepening meditative states through conscious sound awareness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Breath awareness, sound-modulated exhalation, and energetic focus from the heart center up to the crown of the head.
commentary_faqs.answer: Prana-sanchara and Rechaka-kriya focusing on internal resonance (sabda-yoga) within the subtle energy channels (nadis).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Provides a somatic-psychological framework for regulating the autonomic nervous system via controlled exhalation and acoustic feedback, reducing anxiety and improving autonomic balance.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding the word 'punar' (again) - 'tadvat' means in the same way as before; one should perform rechaka (exhalation) and perform puraka (inhalation) repeatedly. He offers an example for the meaning mentioned - 'yathaiva' (just as). Just as the bhastra (bellows), the leather instrument used by a blacksmith for blowing fire, is moved with a certain speed by the blacksmith, who is the creator of iron works.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama (Breath Control)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse outlines the foundational rhythm of Pranayama, emphasizing the cyclical nature of breath control. By alternating exhalation (rechaka) and inhalation (puraka), the practitioner purifies the nadis and steady the mind.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In contemporary yoga practice, this teaches the importance of consistency and regularity in meditative breathing to manage physical stress and psychological volatility.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice is 'Sadhana' of rhythmic, repetitive breath cycles, characterized by 'vega' (controlled speed) and persistence.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around 'Rechaka' (exhalation) and 'Puraka' (inhalation) as dynamic forces, akin to the bellows ('bhastra') which regulate the 'agni' (internal fire/vitality) within the body.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this rhythm acts as a bio-feedback mechanism to regulate the autonomic nervous system, effectively transitioning the mind from a state of 'fight-or-flight' to a state of parasympathetic recovery.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama / Yoga Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights the role of conscious intent in yogic practice. It suggests that the movement of prana is not merely mechanical but must be governed by the 'dhi' (higher intellect) to achieve physiological control.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This emphasizes the mind-body connection foundational to Hatha Yoga, moving from simple physical activity to meditative control.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama, Dharana (focused attention), and subtle energy manipulation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Prana-sanchalana (movement of breath) guided by Dhi (buddhi/intellect) refers to the internal regulation of subtle energy.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Translates to 'conscious regulation of the nervous system' through breathwork and mindfulness, reducing stress and enhancing cognitive regulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Hatha Yoga Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the dual nature of yogic breathing, where the mechanical filling of the abdominal cavity with breath (prana) eventually results in a state of physical and mental lightness (laghava). It emphasizes the transformation of gross bodily sensations through the regulation of internal air.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern terms, this relates to diaphragmatic breathing and its impact on the autonomic nervous system, promoting stress reduction and a sense of 'lightness' or ease in the practitioner's physical and emotional state.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practices prescribed include Rechaka (exhalation), Puraka (inhalation), and the strategic use of Buddhi to monitor the duration and rhythm of breath movement.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on Prana-Sanchalana, where the yogi uses Buddhi (intellect) to consciously regulate Vayu (vital air) within the internal Sthula-sharira (gross body) to achieve physiological balance.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological health benefits from this 'breath-awareness' as a tool for grounding and mindfulness, effectively using the breath-body connection to alleviate anxiety and somatic heaviness.

commentary_faqs.answer: The verse details the mechanical process of Kumbhaka followed by controlled exhalation. It emphasizes that yogic breath regulation is not merely physical, but follows specific energetic patterns (Ida Nadi) to balance the system.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This illustrates the systematic approach of Hatha Yoga towards physiological regulation. It remains foundational for contemporary mindfulness and stress-reduction practices that leverage autonomic nervous system control.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices: Kumbhaka (retention), Rechaka (exhalation), and Nadi-alignment via the Ida channel.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Prana-nirodha' (restraint of vital energy) via 'Kumbhaka'. By utilizing 'Ida', the practitioner invokes the 'Chandra Nadi' (lunar channel) to achieve 'Sheetalata' (cooling) and internal equilibrium.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological health views this as an 'Autonomic Nervous System reset.' The focus on deliberate exhalation through the left nostril (associated with the parasympathetic nervous system) helps mitigate fight-or-flight responses and chronic anxiety.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
क्षिप्रं शीघ्रं कुण्डल्याः सुप्तायाः बोधकं बोधकर्तृ पुनातीति पवनं पवित्रकारकं सुखं ददातीति सुखदं हितं त्रिदोषहरत्वात् सर्वेषां हितं सर्वदा च हितम् । सर्वेषां कुम्भकानां सर्वदा हितत्वेऽपि सूर्यभेदन-उज्जायिनौ उष्णौ प्रायेण शीते हितौ । सीत्कारीशीतल्यौ शीतले प्रायेण उष्णे हिते । भस्त्राकुम्भ्कः समशीतोष्णः सर्वदा हितः । सर्वेषां कुम्भकानां सर्वरोगहरत्वेऽपि सूर्यभेदकं प्रायेण वातहरम् । उज्जायी प्रायेण श्लेष्महरः । सीत्कारीशीतल्यौ प्रायेण पित्तहरे । भस्त्राख्यः कुम्भकःत्रिदोषहर इति बोध्यम् । ब्रह्मनाडी सुष्म्ना ब्रह्मप्रापकत्वात् । तथा च श्रुतिः
‘शतं चैका च हृदस्य नाड्यः तासां मूर्धानमभिनिस्सृतैका ।
तस्याः मुखे अग्रभागे संस्थः सम्यक् स्थितः यः कफादिरूपः अर्गलः प्राणगतिप्रतिबन्धकः तस्य नाशनं नाशकर्तृ ॥ ६६ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Swiftly: immediately. Awakener: the agent that awakens the dormant Kundalini. Purifying: because it cleanses, it is called Pavana (air/purifier). It gives happiness, thus it is 'Sukhada'. Wholesome: because it destroys the three doshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha), it is beneficial to all at all times. Although all Kumbhakas are generally beneficial, Suryabhedana and Ujjayi are hot and generally beneficial in cold conditions. Sheetkari and Sitali are cold and generally beneficial in hot conditions. Bhastra-Kumbhaka is balanced and beneficial at all times. While all Kumbhakas remove diseases, Suryabhedana specifically removes Vata, Ujjayi removes Kapha, and Sheetkari/Sitali remove Pitta. Bhastra is known to be Tridoshahara (destroyer of the three doshas).

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: क्षिप्रम् अर्थात शीघ्र। कुण्डलीबोधकम् का अर्थ है सुप्त कुण्डलिनी को जाग्रत करने वाला। पवन अर्थात पवित्र करने वाला। सुखदं अर्थात सुख देने वाला। हितम् अर्थात त्रिदोषहर होने के कारण सबके लिए हितकारी। यद्यपि सभी कुम्भक हितकारी हैं, फिर भी सूर्यभेदन और उज्जायी उष्ण होने के कारण शीतकाल में हितकर हैं। सीत्कारी और शीतली शीतल होने के कारण ग्रीष्म में हितकर हैं। भस्त्रा कुम्भक सम-शीतोष्ण होने के कारण सदैव हितकर है। सूर्यभेदन वातहर है, उज्जायी श्लेष्महर है, सीत्कारी और शीतली पित्तहर हैं, तथा भस्त्रा त्रिदोषहर है, ऐसा जानना चाहिए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Kundalini Awakening
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that authentic yogic breathing is not merely mechanical but must possess the qualities of awakening latent energy (Kundalini), promoting well-being, and being health-conducive. True practice harmonizes the physiological system to facilitate spiritual transformation.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This underscores the holistic approach of Hatha Yoga, where physical health is treated as a foundational prerequisite for the ascent of consciousness, a principle increasingly recognized in modern somatic therapy.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The text prescribes specific Pranayamas: Suryabhedana, Ujjayi, Sheetkari, Sitali, and Bhastra, recommending their selection based on environmental temperature and the practitioner's specific doshic imbalances.
commentary_faqs.answer: The bhashya defines the breathing technique as a 'Tridoshahara' (the remover of the three biological humors: Vata, Pitta, Kapha), ensuring physiological homeostasis as a prerequisite for 'Kundalini-bodha' (awakening of primordial energy).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this text emphasizes the regulation of the autonomous nervous system. Modern practice translates these as biofeedback techniques where breath modulation directly influences systemic health, emotional stability, and stress reduction.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: That which is firmly established within the body, specifically in the Sushumna nadi, is the 'samudbhuta' (what has arisen). The 'traya of granthis' consists of the Brahma-granthi, Vishnu-granthi, and Rudra-granthi. This (Kumbhaka) is the specific destroyer/piercer of those knots. Therefore, this is known as 'Bhastra' (Bellows breath); this Kumbhaka must be performed with great care and is essentially mandatory. Practices like Surya-bhedana should be performed as feasible. Now, the Bhramari (breath) is discussed.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Kundalini Yoga / Hatha Yoga Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the physiological and subtle-body impact of a specific Kumbhaka (breath retention), which serves to pierce the psychic knots of Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra, thereby allowing the ascent of Prana.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the ancient understanding of subtle body energetics, which aligns with modern interest in somatic mindfulness and the connection between physiological breathing and psychological blockages.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is the Bhastrika-Kumbhaka, characterized as 'avashya-kartavyam' (obligatory/must be done) for the activation of the Sushumna channel.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on the Granthis (psychic knots) which represent existential attachments to Brahma (creation), Vishnu (maintenance), and Rudra (dissolution), requiring systematic piercing through Pranayama.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a secular psychological perspective, these 'knots' correspond to deep-seated behavioral and emotional patterns or nervous system blockages that restrict one's awareness and emotional bandwidth, which rhythmic breathing techniques aim to release.

commentaries.description:
भ्रामरीकुम्भकमाह - वेगादिति । वेगात् तरसा घोषं सशब्दं यथा स्यात् तथा भृङ्गस्य भ्रमरस्य नाद इव नादो यस्मिन् कर्मणि तत् तथा पूरकं कृत्वा । भृङ्ग्यः भ्रमर्यः तासां नाद इव नादो यस्मिन् तत् तथा मन्दं मन्दं रेचकं कुर्यात् । पूरकानन्तरं कुम्भकस्तु भ्रामर्याः कुम्भकत्वादेव सिद्धः अविशेषाच्च नोक्तः । पूरकरेचकयोस्तु विशेषोऽस्तीति तावेव उक्तौ । एवमुक्तरीत्या अभ्यसनम् अभ्यासः तस्य योगो युक्तिः तस्माद् योगीन्द्राणां चित्ते कदाचित् अनिर्वाच्या आनन्दे लीला क्रीडा आनन्दलीला जाता उत्पन्ना भवति ॥ ६८ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary defines the Bhramari Kumbhaka: 'Vegāt' means performing the inhalation with speed and audible sound, specifically mimicking the humming of a male bee (bhṛṅga). Then, one should perform the exhalation (rechaka) slowly and gently, mimicking the humming of a female bee (bhṛṅgī). The retention (kumbhaka) between inhalation and exhalation is implicitly established by the nature of Bhramari itself and is therefore not explicitly detailed. Only the inhalation and exhalation, which have distinct characteristics, are described. Through such practice (abhyāsa), a profound, indescribable joy and play of bliss (ānanda-līlā) manifests in the hearts of great yogis.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Bhramari Pranayama
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the technique of Bhramari Pranayama, a vital yogic practice aimed at stabilizing the mind through sound resonance. By mimicking the subtle humming of bees, the practitioner induces a state of deep internal vibration that calms the nervous system and fosters meditative absorption.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Bhramari is widely recognized today as an effective tool for stress reduction and autonomic nervous system regulation. Its focus on acoustic vibration makes it highly compatible with modern sound therapy and mindfulness-based interventions.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama, specifically Bhramari, emphasizing the distinction between fast/loud inhalation (puraka) and slow/soft exhalation (rechaka) to create internal vibration.
commentary_faqs.answer: Bhramari-kumbhaka is characterized by the resonance of nada (sound vibration), specifically aiming at the citta-vṛtti-nirodha (cessation of mental fluctuations) through the sonic modulation of the inhalation and exhalation.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Vagus nerve stimulation through humming; utilizing acoustic bio-feedback to reduce anxiety, enhance parasympathetic response, and achieve rapid transition into a meditative state.

commentaries.description:
मुर्च्छाकुम्भकमाह - पूरकान्त इति । पूरकस्य अन्ते अवसाने अतिशयेन गाढं गाढतरं दृढतरं जालन्धराख्यं बन्धं बद्ध्वा शनैः मन्दं मन्दं रेचयेत् । इयं कुम्भिका मुर्च्छानाख्या मूर्च्छना इति आख्या यस्याः इति मूर्च्छनाख्या । कीदृशी? मनोः मूर्च्छयति इति मनोमूर्च्छा ।
एतेन मूर्च्छनायाः विग्रहदर्शनपूर्वकं फलमुक्तम् । पुनः कीदृशी? सुखप्रदा सुखं प्रददातीति सुखप्रदा ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Describing 'Murcha Kumbhaka' (fainting breath) - 'At the end of Puraka'. At the conclusion of inhalation, one should apply the bandha known as Jalandhara with extreme firmness. Then, slowly, exhale. This is known as Murcha Kumbhaka, the one that makes the mind swoon/faint (manomurcha). Through this, the fruit of Murcha is explained along with its analysis. Furthermore, it is described as 'Sukhaprada' - that which grants bliss/happiness.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Pranayama (Bandha)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse prescribes the precise application of Jalandhara Bandha to seal the energy (Prana) retained after inhalation. This is a foundational technique to regulate internal pressure and prepare the mind for states of deep suspension.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These techniques are essential for psychosomatic regulation. In modern life, they serve as methods to transition from sympathetic dominance (stress) to parasympathetic regulation (calmness).

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Puraka (Inhalation), Jalandhara Bandha (Throat lock), and controlled, slow Rechaka (Exhalation) as part of the Murcha Kumbhaka technique.
commentary_faqs.answer: Murcha Kumbhaka involves the technical synthesis of Jalandhara Bandha to induce Manomurcha, a state where the chitta (mind) enters a tranquil, suspended state, leading to inner Sukha.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychology identifies these techniques as 'vagal braking' mechanisms, where physical locks and breath retention modulate the autonomic nervous system to reduce cognitive load and emotional reactivity.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text explains the Plāvini Kumbhaka: 'Antaḥ' etc. He who has circulated (pravartita) and filled (pūrita) the great (udāra) wind (māruta) within the body, and thereby filled his belly (udaram) completely (samantāt); such a person floats (plavate) on water (payasi) even if it is bottomless (atalasparśe), with ease (sukhāt) and without effort (anāyāsāt), like a lotus leaf (padmapatravat) resting on the surface.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Plāvini Kumbhaka (Pranayama technique)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the physical state of a practitioner during Plāvini Kumbhaka, where the belly is filled with air to achieve buoyancy. It signifies the mastery over Vayu (prana) to influence the body's density and interaction with water.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This illustrates the Hatha Yoga tradition's focus on physiological mastery. It reminds us that internal regulation of breath can alter physical constraints, useful for understanding mind-body control in modern psychosomatic practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice involves Kumbhaka (retention of breath) specifically directed to distend the stomach with air, facilitating buoyancy.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Plāvini Kumbhaka, focusing on Vayu-Niyantrana (control of breath) to achieve lightness (Laghima) of the physical form.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in the study of 'bio-feedback' and how conscious respiratory control influences physical stability and floating capabilities in therapeutic aquatic environments.

commentaries.description:
अथ प्राणायामभेदानाह - प्राणायाम इति । प्राणस्य शरीरान्तःसञ्चारिवायोः आयमनं निरोधनमायामः प्राणायामः । प्राणायामलक्षणमुक्तं गोरक्षनाथेन - ‘प्राणः शरीरजो वायुरायामः तन्निरोधनम् । ’ (गो.श.४२) इति । रेचकश्च पूरकश्च कुम्भकश्च तैः भेदैः त्रिधा त्रिप्रकारकः, रेचकप्राणायामः, पूरकप्राणायाम;, कुम्भ्कप्राणायामश्चेति । रेचकलक्षणमाह याज्ञवल्क्यः - ‘बहिर्यद्रेचनं वायोः उदराद्रेचकः स्मृतः’इति । रेचकप्राणायामलक्षणम् -
‘निष्क्रम्य नासाविवरादशेषं प्राणं बहिः शून्यमिवनिलेन ।
पूरकलक्षणम् - ‘बाह्यादापूरणं वायोः उदरे पूरको हि सः’ । पूरकप्राणायामलक्षणम् -
‘बाह्ये स्थितं प्राणपुटेन वायुमाकृष्य तेनैव शनैः समन्तात् ।
कुम्भकलक्षणम् - संपूर्य कुम्भाद्वायोः धारणं कुम्भको भवेत्’ ।
अयं कुम्भकस्तु पूरकप्राणायामादभिन्नः । भिन्नस्तु -
‘न रेचको नैव च पूरकोऽत्र नासापुटान्तस्थितमेव वायुम् ।
अथ प्रकारान्तरेण प्राणायामं विभजते - सहित इति । कुम्भको द्विविधः । सहितः केवलश्चेति मतोऽभिमतो योगिनामिति शेषः । तत्र सहितो द्विविधः । रेचकपूर्वकः, पूरकपूर्वकश्च इति । तदुक्तम् - ‘आरेच्यापूर्य वा कुर्यात् स वै सहितकुम्भकः’ । तत्र रेचकपूर्वकः रेचकप्राणामादभिन्नः । पूरकपूर्वकः कुम्भकः पूरकप्राणायामादभिन्नः । प्रागुक्ताः सूर्यभेदनादयः पूरकपूर्वकस्य कुम्भकस्य भेदाः ज्ञातव्याः ॥ ७१ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary introduces the divisions of Pranayama. The term 'Pranayama' is defined as the restraint (nirodhana) of the air moving within the body. Gorakshanatha defines it as 'Prana is the air born of the body; restraint thereof is Ayama.' These three types are Rechaka, Puraka, and Kumbhaka. Rechaka is the expulsion of breath from the belly; Puraka is the filling of the belly with external air. Kumbhaka is defined as the holding of air after filling the vessel (kumbha/body). The commentary further notes the distinction between 'Sahita' (assisted) and 'Kevala' (isolated) Kumbhaka, categorizing the practice into technical sub-types to deepen the practitioner's control.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: टीका प्राणायाम के भेदों का निरूपण करती है। 'प्राणायाम' का अर्थ शरीर के भीतर संचार करने वाली वायु का निरोधन (नियंत्रण) है। गोरखनाथ ने कहा है - 'प्राण शरीर में उत्पन्न वायु है, और उसका निरोधन ही आयाम है।' ये तीन भेद रेचक, पूरक और कुम्भक हैं। रेचक का अर्थ उदर से वायु का निष्कासन है, पूरक का अर्थ बाहरी वायु से उदर को भरना है, और कुम्भक का अर्थ कुम्भ के समान वायु को धारण करना है। टीका आगे 'सहित' और 'केवल' कुम्भक के भेदों का भी उल्लेख करती है, जो योग साधना में दक्षता के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama (Regulation of Life-Force)
commentary_faqs.answer: Pranayama represents the foundational technique in Hatha Yoga for mastery over the autonomic nervous system and the mind by manipulating the flow of prana. Through the triadic structure of exhalation, inhalation, and retention, the practitioner transitions from erratic, unconscious breathing to a state of deliberate, regulated awareness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern life, this practice serves as a direct psychological intervention to mitigate stress, enhance concentration, and improve physiological regulation, bridging ancient somatic discipline with modern mindfulness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice involves the technical sequence of Rechaka (exhalation), Puraka (inhalation), and Kumbhaka (retention), further divided into Sahita and Kevala variations.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Pranayama is defined as 'prāṇasyāyamanam' - the regulation or restraining of vital energy, serving as the bridge between gross physical breath and the subtle state of citta-vṛtti-nirodha (cessation of mental fluctuations).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents 'respiratory biofeedback'. By voluntarily slowing the breath through these three phases, one modulates the parasympathetic nervous system, effectively reducing cortisol and promoting emotional regulation.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: सहितकुम्भकाभ्यासस्य अवधिमाह - यावदिति । केवलस्य केवलकुम्भकस्य सिद्धिः केवलसिद्धिः यावत् यावत् पर्यन्तं स्यात् तावत् तावत् पर्यन्तं सहितकुम्भकं सूर्यभेदादिकम् अभ्यसेदनुतिष्ठेत् । सुषुम्नाभेदानन्तरं यदा सुषुम्नान्तः षट्शब्दा भवन्ति तदा केवलकुम्भकः सिद्ध्यति । तदनन्तरं सहितकुम्भका दश विंशतिः वा कार्याः । अशीतिसङ्ख्यापूर्तिः केवलकुम्भकैरेव कर्तव्या । सति सामर्थ्ये केवलकुम्भका अशीतेरधिका कार्याः । केवलकुम्भकस्य लक्षणमाह - रेचकमिति । रेचकं पूरकं मुक्त्वा त्यक्त्वा सुखमनायासं यथा स्यात् तथा वायोः धारणं वायुधारणं यत् ॥ ७२ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Explaining the duration of Sahita Kumbhaka practice: 'Until' (yāvat). 'Kevalasiddhi' means the perfection of Kevala Kumbhaka. As long as that perfection is not attained, one should practice Sahita Kumbhaka (like Suryabhedana, etc.). When, after piercing the Sushumna, the 'six sounds' occur within the Sushumna, then Kevala Kumbhaka is perfected. Thereafter, ten or twenty Sahita Kumbhakas should be performed. The completion of eighty counts must be done through Kevala Kumbhakas alone. If one has the strength, more than eighty Kevala Kumbhakas should be performed. Explaining the characteristic of Kevala Kumbhaka: It is the retention of breath, done with ease, having abandoned both exhalation and inhalation (Rechaka and Puraka).

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: सहित-कुम्भक के अभ्यास की अवधि बताते हैं - 'यावत्' इत्यादि। केवलसिद्धि का अर्थ है 'केवल कुम्भक' की सिद्धि। जब तक केवल कुम्भक सिद्ध न हो, तब तक सहित कुम्भक (जैसे सूर्यभेदन आदि) का अभ्यास करना चाहिए। सुषुम्ना के भेदन के अनन्तर जब सुषुम्ना के भीतर छः प्रकार की ध्वनियाँ सुनाई देती हैं, तब केवल कुम्भक सिद्ध होता है। उसके बाद दस या बीस सहित कुम्भक करने चाहिए। अस्सी की संख्या की पूर्ति केवल कुम्भक से ही करनी चाहिए। सामर्थ्य होने पर अस्सी से अधिक केवल कुम्भक करने चाहिए। केवल कुम्भक का लक्षण बताते हैं - रेचक और पूरक का त्याग करके, सुखपूर्वक अर्थात अनायास ही वायु का जो धारण है, वही 'केवल कुम्भक' है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Gradual Mastery in Pranayama
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the necessity of a structured progression in Hatha Yoga. It highlights that the advanced stage of 'Kevala Kumbhaka' (spontaneous retention without inhalation or exhalation) can only be reached through the dedicated foundation of 'Sahita Kumbhaka' (controlled regulated breath).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This principle serves as a safeguard against premature advancement in meditative practices, emphasizing that internal states are built upon the habituation of physical and subtle bodily regulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is the repetitive and disciplined application of 'Sahita-Kumbhaka' as a preparatory phase, transitioning into the spontaneous, effortless 'Kevala-Kumbhaka' once internal refinement is achieved.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Kevala-Siddhi' implies the state of 'Kumbhaka' reached through the internalizing of 'Prana' by surpassing the duality of 'Rechaka' (exhalation) and 'Puraka' (inhalation), ultimately leading to the 'Nada' (six sounds) manifestation.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the value of iterative skill acquisition. By mastering controlled, conscious inputs (Sahita), one facilitates the neurological and physiological capacity for spontaneous rest (Kevala), effectively managing nervous system regulation in a high-stress modern environment.

commentaries.description: प्राणेति । स वै इति । निश्चितं केवलकुम्भकः प्राणायाम इत्ययमुक्तः । केवलं प्रशंसति - केवल इति । रेचो रेचकः, रेचश्च पूरकश्च रेचपूरकौ ताभ्यां वर्जिते रहिते केवले कुम्भके सिद्धे सति ॥ ७३ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Prana (vital air) etc. 'That indeed'—this implies that the Kevala-kumbhaka is definitively proclaimed as the true Pranayama. 'Kevala' praises it as absolute. When Rechaka (exhalation) and Puraka (inhalation) are abandoned or absent, and that absolute Kumbhaka (retention) is attained, that state is referred to.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Kevala-Kumbhaka (Supreme State of Pranayama)
commentary_faqs.answer: Kevala-kumbhaka signifies the cessation of breath that occurs spontaneously without the voluntary efforts of inhalation (puraka) or exhalation (rechaka). It represents the highest stage of yogic breath control where the duality of the breath cycle dissolves into a unified state of stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern life, this concept highlights the psychological shift from constant 'active doing' to 'witnessing being'. It serves as a methodology for achieving mental equilibrium by transcending the physiological oscillations of the nervous system.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is the abandonment of the binary effort of inhalation and exhalation, leading to the spontaneous cessation of breath known as Kevala-kumbhaka.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on the state of Kevala-kumbhaka as the culmination of Hatha Yoga practice, distinct from Sahita (coupled) pranayama. It emphasizes the 'Nirapeksha' (independent) nature of this retention, transcending the binary of 'rechaka-puraka' as mentioned in the Bhashya.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the transition from cognitive control to biological stillness. It mirrors the 'flow state' where the individual's effort disappears, replaced by an automatic, rhythmic physiological harmony that reduces stress and heightens awareness.

sanskrit_shloka: न तस्य दुर्लभं किञ्चित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ।
text: न तस्य दुर्लभं किञ्चित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ।
transliteration: na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate.
translation: For that person, nothing is unattainable in the three worlds; everything is easily accessible.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.description: For that person, nothing is unattainable in the three worlds; everything is easily accessible.

translations.description: उस (योगी) के लिए तीनों लोकों में कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है; सब कुछ उसके लिए सुलभ है।
translations.text: उस (योगी) के लिए तीनों लोकों में कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है; सब कुछ उसके लिए सुलभ है।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: नेति । तस्य योगिनः त्रिषु लोकेषु दुर्लभं दुष्प्रापं किञ्चित् किमपि न विद्यते, तस्य सर्वं सुलभमित्यर्थः । शक्त इति । केवलकुम्भकेन कुम्भकाभ्यासेन शक्तः समर्थः यथेष्टं यथेच्छं वायोः धारणं वायुधारणं तस्माद् वायुधारणात् ॥ ७४ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: ‘Na’ (Not). For that Yogi, there is nothing in the three worlds that is ‘durlabham’ (difficult to obtain or unreachable). The meaning is that everything is easily accessible to him. ‘Shaktah’ (Capable): Through the practice of Kevalakumbhaka (retention of breath without inhalation or exhalation), one becomes capable and powerful in holding the Vayu (breath/life force) as desired. From that Vayudharana (breath retention), all becomes possible.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Siddhi and Mastery over Nature through Yoga
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the state of a Yogi who has attained complete mastery over the life force (Prana). Because the mind and reality are interconnected, the removal of internal blockages through Yoga makes all external goals achievable.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the psychological potential of total focus. In modern terms, it reflects the power of flow states and disciplined willpower to overcome environmental limitations.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Kevalakumbhaka and Vayudharana are the specific practices prescribed to reach this state of absolute capability.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Siddhi arising from Vayudharana (control of prana), where the Yogi transcends the limitations of space and objective reality through the refinement of the internal psychic current.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological interpretation suggests that complete regulation of the autonomic nervous system through breath control (Vayudharana) leads to cognitive mastery and the removal of the perceived barriers that limit human potential.

translations.text: निसंदेह वह राजयोग पद को प्राप्त करता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं है।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: राजयोगपदं राजयोगात्मकं पदं लभते । अत्र संशयो नास्ति । निश्चितमेतत् इत्यर्थः । कुम्भकाभ्यासस्य परम्परया कैवल्यहेतुत्वमाह - कुम्भकादिति । कुम्भकात् कुम्भकाभ्यासात् कुण्डली आधारशक्तिः तस्याः निद्राभङ्गो भवेत् । कुण्डल्याः बोधः कुण्डलीबोध; तस्मात् कुण्डलीबोधतः सुषुम्ना मध्यमनाडी अनर्गला कफाद्यर्गलरहिता भवेत् । हठस्य हठाभ्यासस्य सिद्धिः प्रत्याहारादिपरम्परया कैवल्यरूपा सिद्धिः जायते ॥ ७५ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The term 'Rajayogapadam' means the state characterized by Raja Yoga. 'Natrasamshayah' means there is no doubt; it is certain. The text explains that the practice of Kumbhaka leads to Kaivalya (emancipation) through a sequence: Kumbhaka, through constant practice, causes the breaking of the 'sleep' of the Kundalini (the basal power). Kundali-bodha, or the awakening of this power, makes the Sushumna (the central channel) unobstructed—meaning free from the blockages of phlegm and other impurities. Through the practice of Hatha, one eventually attains Siddhi, which is the state of Kaivalya attained through the sequence of Pratyahara and other stages.

commentaries.description: राजयोगपद का अर्थ है राजयोग रूपी पद। 'नात्र संशयः' का अर्थ है यहाँ कोई संदेह नहीं है; यह निश्चित है। कुम्भकाभ्यास की परंपरा से कैवल्य की प्राप्ति का कारण बताते हैं - कुम्भकात्। कुम्भक के निरंतर अभ्यास से कुण्डली (आधारशक्ति) की निद्राभंग होती है। कुण्डली का बोध होने से सुषुम्ना नाडी कफ आदि अवरोधों से मुक्त हो जाती है। हठयोग के अभ्यास से प्रत्याहारादि परंपरा के द्वारा कैवल्य रूपी सिद्धि प्राप्त होती है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Raja Yoga and Kaivalya
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the certainty of reaching the highest meditative state (Raja Yoga) through systematic practice. It posits that the physiological mastery of breath (Kumbhaka) inevitably leads to the awakening of latent spiritual energy (Kundalini), culminating in liberation (Kaivalya).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This highlights the scientific approach of Hatha Yoga where physical discipline is not an end but a bridge to mental stillness, relevant today for stress management and mindfulness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practices are Kumbhaka (breath retention), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), and systematic Hatha yoga, which are essential for removing 'argala' (blockages) in the subtle body.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around 'Kundalini-bodha' (awakening of primordial energy) leading to 'Sushumna-nadi-shuddhi' (purification of the central channel), which culminates in 'Kaivalya' (ultimate liberation) as defined in the context of Hatha and Raja Yoga.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a secular context, this mirrors the psychological process of removing 'mental blockages' or subconscious conditioning. The transition from physical breath control to the 'Raja Yoga' state represents the evolution from physiological regulation to cognitive and emotional homeostasis.

sanskrit_shloka: हठं विना राजयोगो राजयोगं विना हठः ।
text: हठं विना राजयोगो राजयोगं विना हठः ।
transliteration: haṭhaṃ vinā rājayogo rājayogaṃ vinā haṭhaḥ ।
translation: Without Hatha Yoga, Raja Yoga cannot be accomplished; without Raja Yoga, Hatha Yoga cannot be achieved. Thus, one should practice both in conjunction until the highest state is reached.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: हठयोगराजयोगसाधनयोः परस्पर-उपकार्य-उपकारकत्वमाह - हठं विना इति । हठं हठयोगं विना राजयोगो न सिध्यति, राजयोगं विना हठो न सिध्यति । ततः यतः अन्यतरस्य सिद्धिः नास्ति तस्मान्निष्पत्तिं राजयोगसिद्धिम् आ मर्यादीकृत्य या निष्पत्तिः तस्याः राजयोगसिद्धिपर्यन्तं युग्मं हठयोगराजयोगद्वयमभ्यसेत् अनुतिष्ठेत् । हठातिरिक्ते साक्षात् परम्परया वा राजयोगसाधने, अत्र राजयोगशब्दः जीवनसाधने लाङ्गले जीवनशब्दप्रयोगवत् । राजयोगसाधनं चतुर्थोपदेशे वक्ष्यमाणम् उन्मनी-शाम्भवीमुद्रादिरूपम् अपरोक्षानुभूतौ उक्तं पञ्चदशाङ्गरूपम् । वाक्यसुधायाम् उक्तम् दृश्यानुविधादिरूपम् ॥ ७६ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text explains the mutual interdependency between Hatha Yoga and Raja Yoga by stating: Without Hatha, Raja Yoga does not manifest, and vice-versa. Therefore, since the success of one depends on the other, one must practice both as a pair until the final culmination (Rajayogasiddhi). Here, 'Raja Yoga' signifies the ultimate goal of life, akin to how 'ploughing' relates to the 'crop'. The practice of Raja Yoga is defined as the state of Unmani and Shambhavi Mudra, as discussed in the fourth chapter, or the fifteen-fold state described in Aparokshanubhuti.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: यह श्लोक हठयोग और राजयोग की परस्पर पूरकता को बताता है। हठयोग के बिना राजयोग सिद्ध नहीं होता और राजयोग के बिना हठयोग। चूँकि एक की सिद्धि दूसरे पर निर्भर है, इसलिए साधक को अंतिम लक्ष्य 'राजयोगसिद्धि' तक दोनों का अभ्यास युग्म रूप में करना चाहिए। यहाँ राजयोग का अर्थ जीवन का चरम लक्ष्य है। राजयोग के साधन जैसे उन्मनी, शाम्भवी मुद्रा, आदि का वर्णन चतुर्थ उपदेश में किया गया है, जो अपरोक्षानुभूति में वर्णित पञ्चदशाङ्गरूप के समान है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Paraspara-upakāraka (Mutual interdependence of spiritual disciplines)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse posits that bodily mastery (Hatha) and mental-spiritual absorption (Raja) are not separate but mutually supportive. Hatha Yoga provides the energetic container, while Raja Yoga provides the meditative destination; one is the means, and the other is the culmination.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the integration of physical health (holistic wellness) and mental clarity (mindfulness). In a modern context, it suggests that psychological well-being is intrinsically linked to physiological regulation, preventing the compartmentalization of mind and body.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Yugmābhyāsa (paired practice of physical energetic locks and meditative absorption) until the attainment of Unmanībhāva.
commentary_faqs.answer: Paraspara-upakārakatvam (Mutual-dependency); the integration of the energetic (haṭha) and the cognitive (rājayoga) leads to final liberation.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse advocates for a 'psychosomatic' approach to health, suggesting that cognitive focus (mental health) is fragile without the foundational support of a regulated physiology (physical discipline).

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: हठाभ्यसात् राजयोगप्राप्तिप्रकारमाह - कुम्भकेति । कुम्भकेन प्राणस्य यो रोधः तस्यान्ते मध्ये चित्तमन्तः करणं निराश्रयं कुर्यात् । संप्रज्ञातसमाधौ जातायां ब्रह्माकारवृत्तेः परवैराग्येण विलयं कुर्यादित्यर्थः । एवमुक्तरीत्या अभ्यासस्य योगो युक्तिः तेन । योगः सन्नहनोपायध्यानसङ्गतियुक्तिषु (अ.को. ३.३.२२) इति कोशः । राजयोगपदं राजयोगात्मकं पदं व्रजेत् प्राप्नुयात् ॥ ७७ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The author explains the method of attaining Raja Yoga through Hatha Yoga practice. At the end of the breath restraint (Kumbhaka), one should make the 'citta' (mind-instrument) devoid of any reliance. The meaning is that after the Samprajnata Samadhi arises, one should dissolve the 'Brahmakara-vritti' (the thought-wave shaped like Brahman) through Paravairagya (supreme detachment). Through this practice, one attains the state of Raja Yoga.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Citta-vritti-nirodha (Cessation of mental fluctuations)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the state of mind where all external and internal supports for consciousness are withdrawn following the practice of breath retention. By rendering the mind 'nirāśraya' (supportless), the practitioner transcends the dualistic movement of thought, paving the way for Samadhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In a modern context, this practice is akin to achieving a state of profound 'mindfulness' or 'de-identification' from external stressors, allowing for psychological stability and inner peace.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Kumbhaka (retention of breath) is the primary physical catalyst, followed by internal withdrawal (Pratyahara/Dharana) and final 'Laya' (dissolution) of the mind.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Niralambana Yoga' or 'Nirashraya Citta', where the consciousness transitions from 'Samprajnata' (objective consciousness) to 'Asamprajnata' (undifferentiated awareness) through the dissolution of 'Brahmakara-vritti' via 'Paravairagya'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a radical psychological tool for 'de-conditioning' the ego from external stimuli, fostering high-level emotional regulation and mental detachment from chaotic life patterns.

sanskrit_shloka: वपुः कृशत्वं वदने प्रसन्नता नादस्फुटत्वं नयने सुनिर्मले ।
text: वपुः कृशत्वं वदने प्रसन्नता नादस्फुटत्वं नयने सुनिर्मले ।
transliteration: vapuḥ kṛśatvaṃ vadane prasannatā nādasphuṭatvaṃ nayane sunirmale ।
translation: Emaciation of the body, pleasantness in the face, clarity of internal sound, and eyes which are perfectly clear: these are the signs of success in Hatha Yoga.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: हठसिद्धिज्ञापकमाह - वपुः कृशत्वम् इति । वपुषो देहस्य कृशत्वं कार्श्यं, वदने मुखे प्रसन्नता प्रसादः, नादस्य ध्वनेःस्फुटत्वं प्राकट्यं, नयने नेत्रे सुष्ठु निर्मले, अरोगस्य भावः अरोगता आरोग्यं, बिन्दोः धातोः जयः क्षयाभावरूपः अग्नेः उदर्यस्य दीपनं दीप्तिः, नाडीनां विशेषेण शुद्धिः मलापगमः, एतत् हठस्य हठाभ्याससिद्धेः भाविन्याः लक्ष्यते अनेन इति लक्षणं ज्ञापकम् ॥ ७८ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding the indicators of Hatha Yoga attainment, it is said: 'Vapuh krishatvam', etc. The emaciation (karsya) of the body, pleasantness (prasada) in the face, clarity (prakatya) of internal sound (nada), the eyes being perfectly clear (sunirmale), the state of being without disease (arogata), the control over Bindu (absence of depletion), the stimulation of the gastric fire (jathara-agni), and the purification of the Nadis (removal of impurities); these are the signs (jnapaka/lakshana) by which the future or attained Hatha Siddhi is identified.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Siddhi-Lakshana (Signs of Yogic Achievement)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse outlines the somatic and subtle physiological markers that indicate a practitioner's progress in Hatha Yoga. It emphasizes that authentic spiritual practice results in the refinement of the physical vessel rather than its mere destruction.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These indicators remain the standard benchmarks for assessing one's balance between physical discipline (tapas) and metabolic health in modern holistic wellness practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Asana for body leanness, Pranayama for Nada-anusandhana and Nadi-shuddhi, and Basti/Dhati-raksana to achieve Bindu-jaya.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on Kayashuddhi (purification of the body) and Pranasamrodha where the Siddhi manifests through metabolic and sensory refinement, specifically the awakening of Jatharagni and Nadi-shuddhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a psychological sense, these signs map to 'Flow State' and the integration of the parasympathetic nervous system, reflecting a calm mind and clear vision as byproducts of deep systemic physical regulation.
